newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-SUAUDEAU STEPS DOWN AS NANTES COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SUAUDEAU STEPS DOWN AS NANTES COACH.

text.p: Nantes coach Jean-Claude Suaudeau, who twice led the Brittany team to the French league title, resigned on Friday.
Suaudeau, 59, will be replaced by Reynald Denoueix, who was formerly in charge of the Nantes training centre.

A moody, often controversial character, Suaudeau spent his whole career in Nantes both as a player and as a coach. He first took the reins of the team in 1981, leading them to their sixth first division crown in 1983.
He stepped down a first time in 1988 to look after the club's youth teams but returned two years later to coach the side which won the league again in 1995.

Known as a talent scout, he discovered Didier Deschamps, Marcel Desailly, Christian Karembeu and Patrice Loko, who all went on to become internationals. He will remain at Nantes as a technical advisor.
